data.raw_text:
Duterte’s “Golden Pillar of the Law(less) Award” shunned. 

In an “expression of disappointment and disgust,” retired Judge Meinrado Paredes returned the Golden Pillar of Law Award conferred to him by the Integrated Bar of the Philippines after learning that former President Rodrigo Duterte received the same recognition. 

In his own words: “This is not a protest but an expression of disappointment and disgust. I am doing this in solidarity with the victims and their relatives of human rights violations,” Paredes said.

Paredes is among the many lawyers who criticised the IBP’s decision to give Duterte the award, reminding them that Duterte’s regime as President was “characterised by the rule of the gun, not of law,” a time when extrajudicial killings and human rights violations ran rampant. Paredes minced no words saying:“He has blood debts. There is no rule of law if human beings are killed without due process.”

An organisation of human rights lawyers, UPLM previously tagged the move as “a mockery of the thousands of individuals who were killed in the drug war and lost a chance to defend their names in court.”
